title: Play starts at once on a 50 track edit, however many clips are up
goal: On a 50 track edit, pressing Space freezes the picture for more than half a second before anything moves, and for most of a second where ten recordings are up. On the 6 minute edit it starts within a twentieth of a second. Pressing Space on a wide edit should feel just as immediate.
notes: Split off an-edit-with-50-tracks-and-100-clips-scrolls-pla (the user's report of a sluggish 50 track edit), whose audits carried "starting play at 0:58 from rest waits about 727 ms" through four passes with no task owning it. Reproduced 2026-11-25 by the triage pass on the probe built from main that morning: a walk with setup {"forget":["all"],"wideEdit":50} and steps wait 3, then {"do":"speed","measure":"play","fromMS":58000,"seconds":3}, the same from 10000, then 58000 again (Scripts/playtest.sh <walk> --no-build). Output: "played 3.0s from 0:58.0 to 1:00.6: 66 of 91 frames shown, 25 dropped, worst gap 858ms, first new picture 858ms after Space"; "from 0:10.0: 73 of 90 frames shown, 17 dropped, first new picture 625ms after Space"; second time at 0:58: 850ms. The same walk with referenceEdit 6: 50, 58, 58 ms and 0 dropped. Main thread is not the hold (longest pass 6 to 25 ms). Not diagnosed. Place to look first, from reading only: the start waits for first frames of every clip (preRollWithSound, capped at 0.8 s), and 0:10 is slow with few clips up. Played end to end from 0:00 the wait is 75 ms (baselines/wide-50.json firstPictureMS), so the resting frames are in hand there: compare.
acceptance: Reproduced with the walk in the notes, and where the wait goes is named with numbers (reads, places in the read queue, the pre-roll wait) at 0:10 and 0:58 before any fix

First new picture at most 100 ms after Space on the 50 track edit at 0:10, 0:30 and 0:58, worst of three runs, at rest for 2 seconds first and right after a jump (today 625 and 858 ms); where ten recordings cannot all be ready, the canvas moves on and says nothing wrong (no flash, no frame from another time) instead of holding
0 frames dropped in the first 3 seconds at 0:10, and the figure at 0:58 stated (today 17 and 25)
The speed walk --wide records time to the first picture from rest at those places, in its baseline, so it cannot grow back unseen
The 6 minute edit starts no later than today (50 to 58 ms) and its sound stays in step; jumping-back-while-playing-walk and the play walks stay green

Audit written under queue/audits/ with before and after numbers. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: From the 50 track task's closing pass, 2026-11-25: one real dropped frame in seven end to end plays (25,459 frames), due at 0:19.7, not seen again in two tries. A drop the line gives no moment for is the clock itself starting late: wall clock less playhead over two steps (about 66 ms) at the end, so the 64 to 70 ms start counts as one dropped frame. Starting on time removes it; if 0:19.7 comes back, it is yours.

Reproduced on the probe (main 215575c02): first picture 863 / 625 / 383 ms after Space at 0:58 / 0:10 / 0:30; 6 minute edit 50 to 58. Traced: at 0:58 the start waits the full 0.8 s cap (805 ms) for frames of clips covered by a full-frame clip, which nothing reads (readyToStartPlaying asks movieFrames, the fetch asks movieFramesSeen); everything seen was in hand at 172 ms. At 0:10 and 0:30 the frames ahead are not in hand at rest: Space opens 6 (5) passes at once, a place in the gate costs 0.1 ms, the file open 5 ms, and decoding each from its key frame on one shared decoder delivers the first frames at 272 to 550 ms (92 to 323 ms); the clock starts at 575 (337) ms.

Built: startReady counts only clips that are seen; passes a start needs are opened at rest (MovieFrameFetcher.readAheadOfRest); speed walk measure 'starts'. Worst of 3, 50 tracks at 0:10/0:30/0:58: rested 58/67/66 ms, 0 dropped; Space the instant the jump's picture is in 311/129/200; in the same breath as the jump 865/536/530.
